build.prompt_version: Trump Diary Weekly Thread Package Prompt v1

week.headline: The twenty-second week of Trump’s second term did not hinge on a single order or speech.
week.summary: The twenty-second week of Trump’s second term did not hinge on a single order or speech. It unfolded instead as a dense layering of decisions that reached into who may belong, who may protest, who may profit, and which stories the country is allowed to tell about itself. Immigration raids, court rulings, corporate retreats from civil-rights commitments, and symbolic edits in the White House all pointed in the same direction: a state more willing to sort people by loyalty and usefulness, and less

thread_states.canonical_name: Uneven resistance by courts, states, legislatures, and civil society

evidence_items.title: Court rulings as part of the week’s landscape
evidence_items.why_it_matters: The presence of court rulings indicates at least partial institutional checking activity, even if the week’s dominant impression is continued hardening rather than successful resistance.

continuity_notes: Marked reborn because resistance is visible again through court action after not being a central recent frame.

Best placed near the end of the chapter or as a qualifying note within executive-overreach material.

week_summary_notes: The week is best framed as an accumulation of mutually reinforcing developments rather than one signature act.
Immigration, anti-equality rollback, and information/memory control form the main triad of explanation.
Executive overreach matters chiefly as the enabling constitutional backdrop, not necessarily as the most vivid surface story.
Corporate accommodation and insider-benefiting logic re-enter the frame, but as a support thread rather than the chapter lead.
Court rulings supply limited resistance and legal friction, yet they do not dissolve the week’s broader direction of state hardening.
Symbolic White House changes are narratively useful because they connect memory politics to visible personalized power.

rewrite_guidance.opening_focus: Open on the week as a layered sorting operation: raids, rights rollback, and symbolic curation all converging on the question of who belongs, who may dissent, and which identities or histories remain officially legible.
rewrite_guidance.closing_focus: Close on the partial but insufficient friction of courts and other institutions, emphasizing that the week’s significance lies less in any single ruling than in the cumulative normalization of unequal belonging and managed public reality.
continuity_emphasis_notes: Stress continuity from prior weeks in immigration as a generalized domestic-control system.
Link civil-rights retreat and symbolic narrative control as parallel ways of narrowing public belonging.
Use executive overreach as the structural condition that lets disparate actions accumulate across domains.
If mentioning corporate behavior, frame it as accommodation to power and selective advantage, not simply business news.
Treat symbolic White House edits as evidence of memory politics with a personalist edge, not as trivia.
